predecessors.name: Azerbaijan Soviet Socialist Republic
predecessors.text: the Azerbaijan SSR, including the Nakhchivan exclave and the Nagorno-Karabakh Autonomous Oblast

ledger.x: 1991: Azerbaijan declares independence.
February 1992: the war for Nagorno-Karabakh becomes a ground campaign.
May 1992: Armenian forces take Lachin and open a corridor to Armenia; Azerbaijan loses control of the district.
April 1993: Armenian forces take Kalbajar from Azerbaijan.
July 1993: Armenian forces take Agdam.
23 August 1993: Armenian forces take Jabrayil and Fuzuli.
August 1993: Qubadli district falls.
29 October 1993: Zangilan district falls.
12 May 1994: the ceasefire ends the First Nagorno-Karabakh War.
1994: Nagorno-Karabakh becomes a de facto state outside Azerbaijan's control.
1994: Nagorno-Karabakh becomes a de facto state outside Azerbaijan's control.
27 September 2020: Azerbaijan opens an offensive.
October 2020: Azerbaijan retakes Jabrayil and Fuzuli.
20 October 2020: Azerbaijan retakes Zangilan.
October 2020: Azerbaijan retakes Qubadli.
8 November 2020: Shusha falls and southern Nagorno-Karabakh is lost.
10 November 2020: the ceasefire ends the Second Nagorno-Karabakh War.
20 November 2020: Armenia hands Agdam back.
25 November 2020: Armenia hands Kalbajar back.
1 December 2020: Armenia hands Lachin back.
19-20 September 2023: Artsakh surrenders and Azerbaijan takes the rest of Nagorno-Karabakh.

wars.name: First Nagorno-Karabakh War
wars.outcome: Armenian-backed forces took Nagorno-Karabakh and, in 1992-1994, the districts around it (about 9% of Azerbaijan outside the enclave); a Russian-brokered ceasefire took effect at 12:01 AM on 12 May 1994 and the Republic of Artsakh stayed 'de facto independent…

wars.name: Second Nagorno-Karabakh War
wars.outcome: Azerbaijan retook Jabrayil, Füzuli and Shusha (named on the page) and, by the Azerbaijan and Artsakh pages' wording, the rest of the southern districts and Hadrut ('72% of the disputed territory'); the ceasefire of 9/10 November 2020 obliged Armenia to hand…

wars.name: September 2022 Armenia–Azerbaijan clashes
wars.outcome: 'Azerbaijani troops taking control of strategic positions deep inside Armenia'; the infobox puts the Armenian territory Azerbaijan occupies at 200 km2, after about 41 km2 taken on 12 May 2021 in Syunik and Gegharkunik.

wars.name: 2023 Azerbaijani offensive in Nagorno-Karabakh
wars.outcome: 19-20 September 2023: Azerbaijan's offensive ended in Artsakh's agreement to disarm; its president signed a decree on 28 September 2023 to dissolve all institutions by 1 January 2024.

certainty.note: The war years: the front in and around Nagorno-Karabakh moved month by month; Azerbaijan's other frontiers (Turkey, Iran, Georgia, Russia) were Soviet-era lines, sharp.
Soviet republic boundaries and the 1994 ceasefire line of contact, then the 2020 ceasefire lines.
